Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National Mahama announces levy on raw cashew exports to fund local processing industry Source : Albert Kuzor 16 November 2026 5:40pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
President John Dramani Mahama has announced plans to introduce a levy on raw cashew exports, with the proceeds channelled into a dedicated fund to support local processors in purchasing nuts for their factories.
He said the proposed measure, which follows a similar policy in neighbouring Côte d'Ivoire, is intended to strengthen Ghana's domestic cashew processing industry and ensure local factories have adequate raw materials to operate throughout the year.
Mr Mahama said this before he commissioned an EXIM Bank-funded NADKANSCO Cashew Processing Limited in Techiman on Monday, November 16, 2026.
President Mahama said Ghana would adopt aspects of Côte d'Ivoire's approach to protecting and developing its cashew processing sector.
He explained that government would also restrict raw cashew exports during the first three months of the harvesting season to give local processors priority in purchasing the commodity.
“So when the season opens, for the first three months of the season, nobody will be allowed to export cashew nuts from Ghana until our local processors have bought enough. When they have bought enough, then we'll open the gates for the excess to go,” he said.
President Mahama said the export levy would complement the proposed restriction by generating additional resources to help local processing companies compete with exporters for raw cashew supplies.
“And so I think we'll implement the same conditions that Ivory Coast is implementing, Côte d'Ivoire. And in addition, we intend to put a levy on any cashew that is exported, like Côte d'Ivoire is doing,” he said.
He added: “And so if we put a levy on any cashew that is going, that money will go back into a fund, and that fund will go back to the local processors to allow them to buy more cashew nuts.”
The President said the measures were necessary to address the challenges facing local processors, particularly the difficulty in securing sufficient quantities of raw cashew nuts to sustain production beyond the harvesting season.
He cited NADKANSCO as an example, noting that although the factory had the capacity to process about 30,000 to 31,000 metric tonnes of cashew annually, its available working capital would only support operations for approximately 60 to 80 days.
“We don't want a factory that will run for 80 days, shut down for the rest of the year, until the next cashew season. NADCANSCO should be able to buy enough cashew and preserve it so that the young people here can have work all the year round,” he said.
President Mahama further announced that government would provide additional financing to Ghana EXIM Bank to on-lend to NADKANSCO to enable it to purchase enough raw cashew nuts for year-round operations.
He said the export restrictions and levy formed part of government's broader efforts to retain more value from Ghana's agricultural produce, expand local manufacturing and create employment opportunities.
